entries.operation: CNB's loader registry, and the native content manager it needs
entries.evidence: measured rather than deferred on style. The registry itself works: a C probe mints a custom asset type id from a name, registers a loader, writes a .cnb of that type, and cna_content_manager_load_foreign_ext calls the loader and hands the object back -- twice for the same name, from the cache, without calling the loader again, which is XNA reference-type caching. What blocks the projection is this binding's own architecture: that retrieval route takes a NATIVE content manager handle, and there is none here. ContentManager in this package is a managed XNB reader that opens the file through TitleContainer and constructs the object in TypeScript, and no cna_content_manager_* route is imported at all. Registering a loader whose product could never be retrieved would be a mechanism with no consumer. Adopting it means projecting CNA's own ContentManager as a second content path with its own cache, which is an architectural decision to take deliberately rather than as a side effect of wanting one registry. The callback shape is not the obstacle: a trampoline holding a napi_ref and a checked slot table would keep void* and function pointers entirely inside the bridge, the same way the text-input subscriptions already do

entries.operation: Exiting a process after cna_game_destroy has refused
entries.evidence: a refused cna_game_destroy is not side-effect-free: a process that ends in that state takes SIGSEGV after its last statement has run, and an explicit process.exit(0) does not avoid it. Measured five ways in one shape -- a game never destroyed exits cleanly, a game destroyed exits cleanly, a refusal that is cleaned up and retried exits cleanly, and a refusal that is left standing crashes whether or not the offending handle was released afterwards -- so the crash belongs to the refusal rather than to a live game at exit. Written up as upstream finding 18. Every probe game in this package destroys its game and asserts the destroy succeeded, and the suites run one game per process, so a regression that starts refusing shows up as a failed assertion and as a non-zero exit code rather than as a passing file that crashes on the way out

entries.operation: GPU instance culling
entries.evidence: the culler runs and keeps everything. Its compute shader tests each instance against the camera's six frustum planes and increments a visible count the CPU uploaded as zero; the count comes back as the instance count in every case, including three instances ten thousand units outside a hundred-unit frustum. Measured on OPENGLES3, the only renderer built here that supports it -- HEADLESS, SOFTWARE and SDL_RENDERER answer NOT_SUPPORTED and the question does not arise. Nothing is announced: is_supported answers true and the unsupported reason is empty, so a game that adopts it pays for the dispatch, the upload and the readback and draws what it would have drawn anyway. Written up as upstream finding 20, with this package's own BoundingFrustum computing the expected count beside each measured one, so the two cullers are compared with each other. One planted defect -- ignoring an instance's world transform -- survives, and that is recorded rather than hidden: while the cull rejects nothing, whether the transform arrived cannot be observed from outside. A repaired culler kills that mutation and fails two of the four asserted rows, which is the point of asserting them

entries.operation: Reading a PBR effect's texture slots back
entries.evidence: the slots have two sources of truth and they never agree. cna_pbr_effect_apply_material writes the C++ effect's texture pointers; cna_pbr_effect_set_texture writes the C API's own retained-handle table, which is the only thing cna_pbr_effect_get_texture reads. Measured identically on HEADLESS and OPENGLES3: a texture applied with a material is invisible to the slot getter, a texture placed through the setter is invisible to the extractor, and applying a material with an empty slot does not clear one the setter filled. So a material carrying a texture cannot be round-tripped through an effect. Written up as upstream finding 19; all three rows are asserted in both suites, and the binding documents on ExtractMaterial that the slots come back empty rather than inventing a Texture2D wrapper for a handle it does not own

entries.operation: The camera use-after-free CNA has today

Reproduced in plain C with no binding involved, backtrace resolved to CNA::Devices::Camera::Camera at Camera.cpp:68. cna-ts runs the crashing sequence in a child process and asserts the child dies, so a repair fails the test rather than passing unnoticed; every probe here that opens the platform camera runs before the first test-backend one

entries.operation: A post-process pass being told why it could not do its work
entries.evidence: the aerial-perspective pass never refuses: a frame missing a depth image, a far plane or the camera's matrices is copied through unchanged and the reason recorded in words. That ladder is qualified as a ladder rather than as one string -- with nothing supplied it says the depth image is missing, with depth and a far plane it says the camera matrices are, and with all three it says nothing at all -- so the reason is asserted to *change* as inputs are supplied, which a constant string could not do. Finding this also closed a real gap in this binding: the post-process frame carried no camera at all, so the passes that rebuild a world position out of the depth image could never do their work through it. It now carries the projection, both inverses, the previous frame's view-projection and whether there was one, each optional and each defaulting to what CNA's own initializer writes

entries.operation: An effect pass: a caller's own Effect run over a frame, borrowed or taken
entries.evidence: two ownership rules, both measured rather than read. A borrowing pass leaves the effect the caller's: reading it four times returns it four times and detaches nothing, SetEffect(null) detaches and setting it back reattaches. An owning pass consumes the handle, which CNA does by releasing it out of its own registry, so the caller's Effect wrapper gives up its child views and stops owning anything, and its Dispose becomes the no-op Dispose always is once a resource has been given away -- established by measuring that CNA refuses the consumed handle with INVALID_HANDLE and that the technique and pass views release cleanly on either side of the consume. The getter is upstream finding 17: its header says the borrow must not be destroyed, and it mints a registered handle anyway, so obeying the header makes cna_game_destroy refuse for the rest of the process. The binding releases it and documents why on itself, and the windowed game's clean shutdown is the other half of that evidence

entries.operation: Area lights: the shading maths, the linearly-transformed-cosine table, and attaching one to a clustered effect
entries.evidence: four of the shading routes are pure functions, so what a lit rectangle does to a surface is checked without one being drawn. Where the maths is closed it is checked exactly: the lobe width is the GGX alpha floored at 0.02, checked at nine roughnesses including the two ends of the clamp and the exact point where the floor takes over; a rectangle's quad is its own four corners at plus and minus each half-extent; a disc's is the rectangle scaled by sqrt(pi)/2, which is the equal-area scale, on both axes and in the light's own plane. A tube is a billboard, and that is asserted as one -- its quad turns with the surface it is seen from, lies in the plane facing that surface, and keeps the cylinder's axis as its long side either way. Where the maths is not closed it is checked as relationships that only the real model satisfies: coverage falls as the lobe widens and a mirror's lobe is almost entirely inside a quad, a lobe pointing away from the quad sees none of it and two-sidedness does not change that -- because two-sidedness is about the QUAD's facing, which is shown separately by winding the same quad the other way and watching only the two-sided light still reach it. Intensity is an exact multiplier, a wider light puts more on the surface, out of range is exactly zero, and a light switched off contributes nothing while remaining a valid light. Metallic and roughness are asserted to reach different places. The table reports the size and sample count the caller chose, its texture is exactly that size, and CNA's own default is larger and better sampled; the four stored terms behave as the model says -- magnitude falls as a surface roughens, the average lobe direction is the normal head-on and leans along the tangent towards grazing, and Fresnel rises towards grazing. Six planted binding defects fail and none survives

entries.operation: Atmospheric rendering: the drawn sky, the captured one, and the environment behind it
entries.evidence: the strongest acceptance in this package. CNA ships the scattering model twice -- once as the GLSL its sky shader runs and once as cna_atmospheric_sky_radiance, evaluated on the CPU without a device -- and ships a third route that says which way a screen point looks. So every texel of a drawn sky has a prediction assembled from two routes that never touch the GPU, and six skies of 1024 texels each are compared against it on a windowed OPENGLES3 renderer under Xvfb: nowhere do the shader and the model differ by more than one part in 255, which is the resolution the target has, and most texels are bit-identical. The picture is a gradient rather than a fill, a sun below the horizon is ten times darker, a sun placed inside the frustum makes that half of the image the bright one while a sun overhead lights both halves to within two per cent, halving the intensity halves every unclipped texel across the whole image, and a change of turbidity moves the drawn picture the same way and by the same amount as it moves the model -- which is asserted rather than a direction guessed here, because near the horizon aerosol both adds scattered light and takes away sunlight. The captured sky is checked without assuming a cube-map convention: six faces of six flat colours seen down six axes produce six different colours, each the middle of its own face and each of the six that were uploaded, and turning the sky a right angle about the up axis moves exactly the four equatorial faces and leaves the two poles. Intensity and tint multiply what was sampled, a skybox with no environment draws nothing and succeeds, and attaching it again brings the same sky back. The environment processor converts a panorama into a cube map, and handing that cube map over with SetOwnedEnvironment consumes it: the wrapper refuses further use and its Dispose becomes harmless. Two ownership traps were found by writing the binding to the header and measuring: cna_skybox_get_environment mints an owned handle whose loss makes the game undestroyable, and cna_render_pipeline_get_skybox documents the same contract and echoes the caller's own handle, so releasing it destroys their skybox -- upstream finding 15, with the binding doing the opposite thing in each case and saying why. Twenty-three planted binding defects fail and none survives

entries.operation: Automatic exposure: measuring a scene and adapting to it
entries.evidence: it measures with a compute shader, so HEADLESS refuses it honestly and the qualification is windowed. Both halves are exact. The measurement is the average channel value: a white scene measures one and a scene of eight-out-of-255 measures exactly that. The adaptation is an exponential approach to key over luminance, and the test predicts every step of it: the exposure after a step is target + (current - target) * exp(-speed * seconds), where the speed is the brightening one when the scene got brighter and the darkening one when it got darker -- five steps towards a bright scene and five towards a dark one, each matching to a ten-thousandth. Around that: the two directions genuinely differ, each approach is monotone and never overshoots, a two-second step travels further than a tenth-of-a-second one and by exactly the amount the rate implies, and an exposure range clamps the result however long it runs and settles on the bound rather than oscillating. CNA's own defaults are a light meter's: an exposure of one, a key of eighteen per cent grey, and adapting to light faster than to dark

entries.operation: Build-time content compilation: source files into .cnb, in a separate package
entries.evidence: The direction docs/content-pipeline-boundary.md chose, built. `cna-ts-content` is a separate package with its own exports, and the runtime tarball contains none of it: the three routes in the whole binding that read a file by path live there and nowhere else, which is what keeps the browser runtime free of filesystem and compiler APIs. Bytes cross that boundary and handles do not -- each operation imports, describes, encodes and releases inside one native call -- so the package owns no native lifetime at all. Proved end to end: a PNG and a RIFF/WAVE file written from their own specifications (not produced by CNA, because an importer test in which CNA reads back its own output proves nothing) are compiled to .cnb, written to disk, and loaded by the real runtime, where the four exact texels and the exact sample bytes come back. The colour key is asserted at the texel: the keyed one becomes transparent and the other three are untouched. Wrong-format sources are refused in both directions, and a planted defect that accepted the colour key without applying it passed until the test stopped varying the content name as well

entries.operation: Camera frame capture
entries.evidence: opening the platform camera succeeds on a host that has none -- CNA documented contract -- and the state is what reports the absence: NotSupported with a 0x0 frame format. CNA own test backend then supplies what the hardware cannot: four distinct pixels published through it arrive in a caller-owned Texture2D with their channels the right way round, a second frame of sixteen different bytes replaces the first, a texture whose size does not match the frame is refused rather than resized, and the frame stays available until it is replaced. Every injectable state round-trips, and CNA refuses Closed and NotSupported for a device it opened. The injection hooks refuse a camera that is not the test backend, so a test cannot fabricate a reading for a real device. Three planted defects -- zeroed pixels, an acquisition that always claims success, and hooks that accept a real camera -- all fail. This is injection evidence, not hardware evidence: a physical camera stays hardware-pending

entries.operation: Cascade splits, spot cones and cube faces: the rest of the shadow-map maths
entries.evidence: a cascaded shadow map's split distances are checked against both closed forms rather than recorded numbers: lambda 0 is the uniform split exactly, lambda 1 the logarithmic one, and lambda 0.5 their midpoint at every cascade -- and the two schemes are asserted to disagree by more than tenfold near the camera, so those are not all the same check. CNA takes two to four cascades and refuses the rest with its own result code. A view frustum yields eight distinct corners and a bounding sphere that encloses them snugly -- the farthest corner is on the surface, not inside it, which is what stops a cascade shimmering as the camera turns. A spot light's view puts the light at the origin, its projection is perspective rather than orthographic, its range lands exactly on the far plane along the cone axis, and a wider outer angle changes the field of view. The six cube faces each put the light at the origin, each look along a unit axis, and form exactly three opposite pairs. The cube projection is ninety degrees and square. Three planted defects fail: a fixed lambda, a cube face that is always face zero, and a fixed cone angle

entries.operation: Clustered lighting: the assignment a GPU would read
entries.evidence: the three views of one assignment -- the per-cluster read, the flat index list and the per-cluster offsets -- are checked against each other for every one of sixty-four clusters, not a sample. The final offset equals the index list length equals the reported total reference count, the offsets never go backwards, and the reported maximum lights per cluster is the largest cluster actually produced. A per-cluster read that ignored its argument and an offset list missing its end marker were both planted and both fail

entries.operation: Clustered lighting: the cluster grid's exact geometry
entries.evidence: all sixty-four clusters of a 4x2x8 grid, each flat index checked against slice * tilesX * tilesY + y * tilesX + x rather than a sample. The depth axis is logarithmic and asserted against the closed form near * (far/near)^(slice/count), and separately asserted not to be the linear spacing, which would otherwise satisfy every weaker check. The projection round-trips: multiplying it by the inverse CNA returns gives the identity to within 1e-5 through XNA own Matrix.Multiply. A planted x/y swap in the index mapping fails this

entries.operation: Clustered lighting: the light set and what CNA refuses to light with
entries.evidence: three lights with three different values in every field, added, read back one at a time and in bulk, replaced, removed and cleared. A point light influence is a sphere on its own position with its own range; a spot influence is its cone bounding sphere, which is somewhere else entirely, and that difference is what shows CNA computing the bounds rather than copying the position -- a planted position-and-range substitution fails it. The two add paths are cross-checked: a point light added through CNA own conversion agrees with the same light built in the uniform shape on every field that has an effect and on the computed bounds, and differs only in the direction and cone angles a point light does not have, which CNA fills with its own canonical defaults rather than zero -- a rule this package hands to CNA rather than restating. CNA refuses a zero or negative range, a negative intensity and a spot whose inner angle is wider than its outer, each with INVALID_ARGUMENT

entries.operation: CNA's content survey: what is under a content root and which XNB readers it needs
entries.evidence: The test builds the root it surveys, from the same fixtures the XNB reader suites use, so the expected reader names are known independently of what the survey answers rather than read back from it. Four assets across two subdirectories come back as the keys ContentManager.Load addresses -- extension stripped, subdirectories kept -- and a loose .png written beside an .xnb is reported as a native extension rather than as a second asset. A texture declares exactly its one reader and a model exactly its five, in the fixture's own order. Reader usage is counted across the whole root: the texture reader is wanted by two files (the atlas, and the model's effect), each distinct name appears once however many files want it, and each carries whether CNA has a reader for it. The limitation is asserted rather than hidden: the same model written twice, raw and LZX-compressed, reports five reader names and none -- the table lives inside the compressed payload and the survey reads headers without decompressing -- so an empty list means unknown, never "needs nothing". An empty root surveys to nothing instead of failing, changing the root re-points the scan, and a name nothing reads answers false rather than throwing. Loading is deliberately absent: CNA's content manager has a cache and an asset identity of its own, and one asset with two owners would break the same-reference guarantee XNA makes and this package's tests pin. See docs/native-content-survey.md

entries.operation: CNB curves and animation clips
entries.evidence: A curve round-trips its two loop modes, its key count and every field of every key, including a continuity that differs between keys -- and then it is checked the way a curve actually matters, by evaluating both the authored and the decoded curve at ten positions including four between the keys, where the tangents and the continuity decide the answer. What comes back is a managed XNA Curve with no native object behind it: the native handle and its key collection are both released inside the decode. An animation clip keeps its handle, because XNA has no clip type to become; its duration, target space, two tracks with different bone indexes and different keyframe counts, and every component of every keyframe -- three vectors of different lengths at different offsets -- are asserted, along with out-of-range refusals and the fact that a curve and a clip refuse each other's containers. Two planted bridge defects, a dropped key continuity and an ignored track index, each fail exactly one test

entries.operation: CNB model: the bone hierarchy, parts and payloads, materials, meshes, skeleton and lights
entries.evidence: CNB's largest schema, read and written through CnbModelData. A reference model with every projected level occupied at once -- two bones in a hierarchy, a part with real vertex and index payloads, a material with distinguishable values in every field and all eight texture slots named differently, a mesh, a skeleton with three matrix sets, a light -- is built with the public API, encoded by CNA's own writer and decoded back. Every assertion is a value: the exact parent links and transforms, the exact payload bytes and lengths, each of the eight texture names through its own slot, the mesh's parent bone and part membership, and all three skeleton matrix sets kept apart by their own diagonals. Refusals are asserted too: another asset type, a corrupted image, a payload that contradicts its declared part (which CNA validates at encode rather than at set, measured rather than assumed), and use after disposal. Two planted bridge defects -- an ignored skeleton matrix-set identity and an ignored texture slot -- each fail exactly one test

entries.operation: CNB sound effects, songs and videos: the compiled media schemas
entries.evidence: A sound effect round-trips its format, rate, channels, frame count, both loop numbers and its sample bytes exactly, and CNA's own WAV decoder reads a RIFF image into one with the same bytes the header declared; a file that is not a WAV is refused. CreateSoundEffectFromCnb produces a real XNA SoundEffect owning a native audio resource whose name round-trips through CNA, and refuses by name for a format XNA cannot represent -- eight-bit PCM read as sixteen would play as noise -- while leaving the samples readable. Songs and videos carry a stream reference rather than the media, so both schemas are complete and fully testable with no encoded audio or video at all: name, duration and stream reference for a song; dimensions, a non-integer frame rate, duration, soundtrack kind and stream reference for a video. Each of the three refuses the other two's containers. entries.operation: CNB's writers: authoring a container for an asset type CNA has no schema for
entries.evidence: one of every primitive the byte writer offers, decoded back at its exact offset with a DataView -- which is what proves the widths and the little-endian order rather than only that some bytes survived. A u64 survives exactly because it crosses as a bigint; a negative i32 is not read as unsigned; a string carries a four-byte length before its UTF-8 bytes. ToArray copies and Take empties, and the two are distinct. A container built from a custom asset type, custom schema version, metadata, an external reference and a game-defined chunk parses back through the same CnbDocument reader every projected schema uses, with the chunk payload byte for byte. CNB validates structure when a chunk is added -- alignment must be a power of two within its ceiling -- and sizes when the document is built, and both halves are asserted where they happen. Four planted defects all fail: a Take that copies, a u16 written at 32 bits, a dropped power-of-two check, and a limit narrowed but never sent

entries.operation: Colour grading through a .cube LUT, as a strip and as a volume
entries.evidence: the acceptance is a table this package wrote and can apply itself. A size-2 .cube whose transfer is the channel rotation (r,g,b) -> (b,r,g) is parsed, every one of its eight corners is read back and checked against that permutation, and it is then handed to a ColorGradePass twice -- once as the 4x2 strip texture CNA builds from it and once as the 2x2x2 volume -- and run over a sixteen-texel gradient on a windowed OPENGLES3 renderer under Xvfb. The rotation is linear in each channel, so trilinear interpolation reproduces it exactly, and every channel of every texel comes back byte-identical to the rotation computed in JavaScript, through both kinds of table, which also proves no flip, mirror or transpose: the source gradient is asserted to be asymmetric under all three first. Strength is a lerp, so half strength is the exact midpoint and zero strength is the exact source, as is a pass with no table at all. LutSizeForStrip is checked against the shape a strip must have -- N slices of N by N -- for six valid sizes and five invalid ones, which are refused with 0 rather than guessed. Text that is not a .cube file is refused by CNA with its own result rather than parsed into a table that would grade nothing, an index outside the cube is refused rather than clamped, and a non-unit DOMAIN is carried through rather than normalised away. One real binding defect was found by running this: the two getters mint different kinds of handle -- a strip comes back as a borrowed render target and a volume as a Texture3D -- and releasing either through the other's route is refused, which is now what the code does and says

entries.operation: Compass and motion sensors: absence, and a real reading through CNA's own injection
entries.evidence: Absence first, and it is the point of the family: a heading of zero and a rotation rate of zero are both perfectly plausible measurements, so all three sensors report NotSupported with no valid data and refuse CurrentValue rather than returning them. Then the data path, through cna_compass_set_test_backend_ext and cna_motion_set_test_backend_ext -- CNA's own synthetic backends -- which is **injection evidence, not hardware evidence**: no physical compass or motion sensor exists on this host. Every component carries a value no other component has, so a transposed or substituted field is visible: two compass headings that differ by the local declination, a magnetometer vector, a 16-value attitude matrix asserted by first row and diagonal, a quaternion, and three motion vectors with disjoint value sets. Timestamps cross as bigints and are asserted to the tick, which a double would lose. The north-reference flag is installed both ways and read back both ways, so it is proved read rather than defaulted. A backend cannot be swapped underneath a running acquisition. Three planted defects each fail the test: two headings read from one field, a transposed attitude matrix, and gravity read from the device acceleration

entries.operation: Compute shaders and storage buffers: exact GPU computation
entries.evidence: a dispatch computes values[i] * uScale + uOffset + i over 64 float elements, and all four inputs are separately load-bearing: every element differs, so a dispatch that did nothing leaves the seed, one that ignored either uniform produces a different sequence, and one that ignored the invocation index produces a constant. Two work groups of sixteen touch exactly the first thirty-two elements, which is what proves the dispatch count reaches the GPU. Measured on OPENGLES3 under Xvfb; HEADLESS, SDL_RENDERER and SOFTWARE refuse every create with NOT_SUPPORTED and that refusal is asserted rather than skipped. A typed buffer refuses an element transfer whose element size disagrees with its own

entries.operation: Contact shadows: the short screen-space ray that catches what a shadow map misses
entries.evidence: the pass's two decisions are published as pure routes, so both are checked against their closed forms without a depth buffer. The occlusion test is a BAND, not a threshold, and every side of it is pinned: a surface does not shadow itself, nor does a ray within the bias of it, a ray behind it by more than the bias and less than the thickness is occluded, and one behind it by more than the thickness has gone around the occluder rather than into it -- which is what stops a contact shadow smearing into a streak behind every object, and is the half a one-sided test would get wrong. Both ends are exclusive, shown at the thickness end where the float arithmetic is exact, and a thickness equal to the bias leaves a band with nothing in it so nothing is ever occluded. The reference is computed in float rather than double, because at a boundary like 1.05 minus 1.0 the two land on opposite sides and the float one is what ships. Combining with a shadow map's own visibility is a clamped product: two half shadows compound rather than one winning, a visibility above one is clamped so it cannot brighten the other, and one below zero is clamped rather than flipping the sign. On a windowed renderer the pass compiles and runs, its own off switch is a byte-exact copy, and it names which input it was missing in a three-state ladder whose second state names the inverse view -- a different input from the one the aerial pass's second state names, so the two ladders are not one string. Five planted binding defects fail and none survives

entries.operation: Custom shader effects: an Effect built from GLSL the game wrote itself
entries.evidence: a ShaderEffect IS an Effect -- asserted with instanceof, and with the one technique and one pass it reports -- so it goes wherever a stock effect goes, which is the whole point of it. All three IEffectMatrices transforms round-trip to distinct values, and are read AGAIN after every uniform setter has run, so a setter wired to one of them instead of to its own uniform is caught. Every uniform shape CNA offers is exercised: mat4, vec4, vec3, vec2, float, int, float array, vec2 array, vec3 array, mat4 array and the std140 block declaration with its clearing form. The refusals are this binding's own and each names a different mistake: an empty or missing uniform name, a value that is not finite, a block whose names and offsets differ in length, and an array argument that is not one. A texture bound to a sampler unit is LENT to the effect -- the texture then refuses disposal while the effect can sample it, and disposes cleanly once the effect is gone, so the order is the only thing that matters -- and on a windowed renderer a texture bound to unit 1 is what a shader sampling unit 1 reads, which a binding that went to unit 0 cannot produce. Nonsense source is handled the way CNA's header says it must be: success means the object exists and not that anything compiled, and the two renderers here disagree exactly as the header predicts -- HEADLESS reports it valid with an empty log because it never compiled it, OPENGLES3 reports it invalid with the compiler's own words. Two empty sources are the one case refused identically everywhere; one empty source is not. On a windowed renderer the effect drives real pixels, and the weighted-blended accumulation it makes possible is predicted channel by channel from the published weight. Upstream finding 22 is asserted rather than worked around: a fresh effect's FIRST SpriteBatch draw produces nothing, its second is correct, a separately created effect loses its own first draw too, the same batch with no custom effect draws correctly the first time, and one Apply outside any batch fixes it -- which is the diagnosis as much as the workaround. Seventeen planted binding defects fail and none survives

entries.operation: Deferred decals: a texture projected onto whatever the prepass drew
entries.evidence: accepted texel for texel, against a prediction that is CNA's own. For every screen texel the test reconstructs the world point the decal shader reconstructs -- the camera is a 90-degree square frustum, so a plane at view depth d spans d world units per unit of device coordinate -- transforms it by the inverse of the box's world matrix and asks cna_decal_pass_is_inside_decal_box whether it lands inside, intersected with the surface the prepass actually rasterised. Five boxes over one surface are each checked against that prediction with an exact texel count and no tolerance at all: the whole rectangle, one half as wide, two small ones in opposite corners that share no texel, and a long box rolled thirty degrees about the view axis that paints a 117-texel diagonal band across the full width -- a shape no axis-aligned box could produce, so the box's rotation demonstrably reaches the projection. A box the surface does not reach paints nothing, and CNA's own box test agrees that it should; a pass with no depth input paints nothing and does not fail. Opacity is checked through the blend rather than through its getter: the pass composites NonPremultiplied, so half opacity over a known clear colour is an arithmetic identity the test computes, including that blend's own alpha rule, and a green tint on a red decal leaves black because the tint multiplies channel by channel. The slope test is semantic: with the prepass normals supplied, a decal projecting the way the surface faces takes none of it and one turned through half a turn takes all of it, and then with the box left exactly where it is, a surface tilted 60 degrees shows, 80 degrees does not, and widening the limit to 85 brings the same picture back -- one number different. Opacity clamps into the unit range, the slope clamps to a right angle and floors at zero, and the tint is taken as given because above one brightens an HDR frame. The input rule is measured rather than left to be discovered: the prepass's own buffers are the depth input and an upload of the same bytes is not, which SetPrepassInputs documents

entries.operation: Frustum culling, and the vertex declarations an instancing stream takes
entries.evidence: the acceptance is two implementations of one predicate, neither derived from the other: CNA's culler and this package's own XNA BoundingFrustum, asked about the same eleven boxes and five spheres built for the same camera. They agree on every one, and the fixture is asserted to be mixed -- neither all visible nor nearly none -- so the agreement cannot be vacuous. The batch routes are checked against the single test rather than against recorded indices: culling a batch keeps exactly what testing them one at a time keeps, in order, and an empty batch keeps nothing. A culler set from one view-projection matrix agrees with one set from two on every case. Culling *transforms* has two traps and both are pinned: the bounds are matched by index and are already world-space, so one shared local box keeps every transform rather than testing them all against it, and a transform with no matching bound is KEPT rather than dropped -- CNA's own header says so, and a caller who miscounted would expect the opposite. Given one world-space bound per transform it answers exactly what culling those bounds answers. The instancing streams are described by CNA rather than written down here: four Vector4 rows on consecutive texture-coordinate channels at sixteen-byte offsets with a stride of sixty-four, and one packed Color for a tint with a stride of four. entries.operation: glTF material extensions: clearcoat, sheen, transmission, iridescence and subsurface
entries.evidence: bound as a handle rather than a value struct because the canonical type holds nine borrowed Texture2D pointers, which do not belong in caller-writable memory -- and it still behaves as a value, which is what is checked: two fresh sets compare equal and hash alike, copying makes an edited set equal to its source and leaves the source alone, and the printed form is {} when neutral and names each feature that is on. The subtle part is what IsNeutral means, and it is measured one field at a time from a fresh set each time: it reports whether a feature *contributes*, not whether a field was written. A sheen colour, a transmission factor, an iridescence factor, a subsurface colour or a clearcoat factor makes the set non-neutral; a sheen roughness, a thickness, a subsurface wrap, a clearcoat roughness or an attenuation distance does not, even though each stores its value and reads back. entries.operation: GraphicsAdapter: the adapter list, its display modes and its format answers
entries.evidence: The one strict XNA type this package projected structurally and could not fill, because nothing read CNA's adapter capabilities. Its fourteen routes are now bound and the type is real on HEADLESS and on three windowed renderers. The read is deliberately lazy: CNA's adapter routes take a *borrowed* graphics-device handle and permit that borrow only inside a lifecycle callback, so a read at device-creation time is refused with INVALID_STATE -- what is registered there is a source, resolved the first time a caller asks, which for a game is from LoadContent. Asserted: one adapter, its four separate integer identity fields, a current display mode whose aspect ratio matches its own dimensions, a supported-mode list, both XNA profiles with HiDef implying Reach, and a 64x multisample request answered inexactly with a count CNA can actually provide. The description and device name are CNA's canonical XNA values rather than a GPU probe -- the same on HEADLESS and OPENGLES3 -- and that is stated rather than dressed up. A renderer with no adapters still refuses by name; a renderer with no native monitor handle answers zero, which is a legal IntPtr, rather than failing the whole adapter. entries.operation: Level-of-detail groups, and the hysteresis that damps a boundary
entries.evidence: levels added out of order come back sorted, and every band is checked on both sides of every threshold -- a threshold ends its level, and past the last one the answer is -1 rather than a clamp to the coarsest. The hysteresis is the part worth proving: with a margin of 3 around a boundary at 25, climbing holds the near level until 28 and descending holds the far one until 22, and the two walks are asserted not to be each other reversed, which is what separates hysteresis from rounding. A jump of more than one level is deliberately undamped, and that is asserted too. Screen-space selection projects radius * (height / 2) / (distance * tan(fov / 2)) exactly, and halving with distance. Three planted defects fail: a Reset that does not forget, a margin that never reaches CNA, and a projection that ignores its distance. Levels now carry a real ModelMeshPart. Select hands back the very public object that was added -- asserted by identity, not by equality -- because a managed part can lend CNA a native view of itself built over the buffers it already owns. entries.operation: Light probe baking: six cube faces rendered per probe, and the probe they produce
entries.evidence: accepted on real captures on a windowed OPENGLES3 renderer under Xvfb. Which face the scene callback is being asked to draw is decided inside the callback by matching the view CNA handed over against what FaceView reports for that face and that capture point, so the callback's own behaviour is the evidence that each face got its own camera -- and a bake that gave one camera to every face, or the six in another order, cannot produce the list the test asserts. Every face is captured through the square 90-degree frustum the test builds itself. Then the acceptance: light exactly one face and the probe is brightest looking that way and a hundredfold darker looking the other, light the opposite face and the two answers swap, light a third and the brightest direction moves with it. Painting the same face at half a byte scales every one of the nine coefficients by that fraction, which is the projection's linearity in radiance measured rather than assumed; an unlit scene bakes a probe that is zero in every direction; a fully lit one bakes an isotropic probe whose direct term is twenty times any other. A two-cell volume is baked with the scene lit only for the cell the callback recognises, and only that cell carries light, so each probe was captured from its own place; the same bake from a point away from the origin produces the same probe. Visibility is a distance rather than a colour: painting every face one known byte records exactly that fraction of the far plane, with the mean squared equal to the mean squared because a uniform face has no variance, and a light bake afterwards keeps every distance. An exception thrown by the scene comes back out of the bake as itself and the device still bakes afterwards, which is what says CNA was not left holding a bound target. HEADLESS cannot read a target back, so its baker reports unsupported, every bake refuses by state, and the scene callback is never called -- asserted rather than skipped, because a bake that drew and threw the result away would look identical from outside

entries.operation: Light probes as values: nine coefficients, six occluder distances, and the grid over them
entries.evidence: checked against arithmetic with every constant measured from CNA rather than written down. A probe's irradiance is a fixed quadratic in the surface normal with five constants, and the test lights one coefficient at a time to read each of them out of CNA -- twice over for the two that appear in more than one term, which have to agree -- then predicts what a probe with all nine distinct coefficients answers for nine normals, and it does, to 1e-4 on every channel. A direct-only probe is identical in every direction, an overshooting fit comes back at zero because negative light is not a look, a degenerate normal is treated as straight up, and scaling multiplies the irradiance with the coefficients. Equality is by content and content includes the position, which the volume's own behaviour then shows: a probe copied into a cell takes the cell's position, so it stops being equal to its source until the source is moved to match. The grid's probe positions are an even step along each axis computed by the test, an axis holding one probe puts it at the box's minimum, and trilinear sampling is exact at a cell, at a half and at a quarter, with a position outside the box clamped in rather than refused. Visibility floors both distances at zero and the mean squared at the mean squared -- no distribution has negative variance -- and the weight is Chebyshev's bound, computed by the test from the numbers it stored: one when nothing is known to be in the way, and a diagonal between two recorded axes mixing both rather than picking either, which is a third number from either alone. Twenty-two planted binding defects fail and none survives

entries.operation: Spatial upscaling
entries.evidence: a four-by-four source whose left half is black and right half white, drawn at eight by eight over a clear colour that is neither -- so anything the pass fails to write shows up as itself, and the edge says where it landed. Every texel of the target is written, every row is the same because the edge is vertical, each row is monotone from black to white, the black side stays black and the white side stays white, and the edge lands halfway across because it was halfway across the source. A flat source would prove none of that: an upscale of a flat field is that field whatever the sizes are. IsIdentityScale is checked as a pure function -- the same size is nothing to upscale, one axis differing is enough, and downscaling is not an identity either. Two mutations in this family survive and are recorded rather than hidden, and both are equivalent rather than gaps: the roll-off is Reinhard, which is symmetric in its two arguments, and IsIdentityScale asks whether two sizes are equal, which is symmetric by nature. Swapping the draw's own sizes, which is not symmetric, is killed
