entries.operation: The .cnj compile front end, and the dependency lists a build system needs
entries.evidence: a .cnj document authored here from its own specification -- so what the runtime decodes is evidence about the compiler rather than CNA agreeing with itself -- compiles into a .cnb the runtime package reads back with every key's position, value and continuity exactly as the JSON declared, and with the loop kinds it named. The content name defaults to the document stem and honours an override. A document naming a PNG sidecar reports both files in AbsorbedFiles, which is the dependency set a build system watches, and the four texels the PNG carried arrive through the compiler unchanged. An unsupported asset type, a missing sidecar and a missing document are each refused with CNA's own IO result rather than a message match, which is what distinguishes CNA refusing from this package refusing first. It lives in cna-ts-content because it takes filesystem paths

entries.operation: The atmosphere's model, its sampling sequence, and the two mappings around a cube map
entries.evidence: everything about the atmosphere that is arithmetic rather than rendering, checked on relationships and identities rather than on recorded numbers. A sun below the horizon leaves a sky twenty times darker than one above it; the horizon is brighter than the zenith because a horizontal ray passes through more air; a clear zenith is blue then green then red, which is Rayleigh's fourth-power wavelength dependence; and aerosol brightens the sky and washes the colour out of it, because Mie's has none. A view direction with no length is treated as straight up, and a direction is a direction whatever its length. The roughness ramp is a straight line between mip zero and the last, inverse in both directions, answering rather than refusing for a chain with nothing to index and clamping a roughness outside the unit range. The Hammersley sequence is checked point by point against its own definition -- evenly spaced along one coordinate, the radical inverse of the index in base two along the other, and no two points sharing it. GGX importance sampling at roughness zero is the normal itself, roughening it spreads the sample further, and every sample is a unit direction inside its normal's hemisphere. The six cube faces look down the six axes; the panorama mapping puts the poles at nought and one, every horizon direction halfway down, opposite axes half a turn apart and perpendicular ones a quarter -- and the two routes are made to agree by sending one's answers into the other. The view ray a screen point looks along is checked as geometry too: the centre looks the way the camera does, the edges are forty-five degrees off a ninety-degree frustum, and a yaw rotates every ray about the up axis by exactly that rotation, which is asserted as a rotation rather than as an angle because a tilted ray sweeps through less than the yaw. The three setters that guard three different ways are kept apart and asserted apart: turbidity clamps into the model's range, a sky's negative intensity keeps the previous value while a skybox's is floored at zero, and a sun direction is normalised with a degenerate one a silent no-op

entries.operation: The canonical PBR material as a value: equality, hashing, printing and device state
entries.evidence: CNA carries the physically-based material in two C shapes -- the layout frozen before the KHR_materials_* factors existed, and the canonical one every accessor on the C++ type corresponds to -- and this projects the canonical one. It is a value and is checked as one: two materials built the same way compare equal and hash alike, one edited field makes them differ and changes the hash, the same edit twice gives the same material again, and two materials never share their per-slot arrays. CNA's own defaults are glTF's -- fully metallic and fully rough, an IOR of 1.5, an opaque white base colour, every slot on UV channel zero with a neutral transform -- and each is asserted against what glTF specifies rather than against a number recorded from a run. The printed form names the fields it carries, including all four channels of a base colour no default equals. What ApplyState does is qualified by reading CNA's device state back rather than by trusting the wrapper's, which cannot see it: a blended material leaves SourceAlpha/InverseSourceAlpha, an opaque or masked one leaves One/Zero, and a double-sided one leaves CullNone -- each predicted from the XNA state the C++ names, not from a measurement. Fifteen planted binding defects fail and none survives

entries.operation: The canonical render-pipeline settings: clamping, quality presets and the settings text
entries.evidence: forty-seven fields, moved through the bridge by three offsetof tables rather than by hand, so a field added upstream is a compile error in the ABI audit rather than a silently dropped value. It is a value and is checked as one: two bags do not share state, and every operation answers a new bag rather than editing the one it was handed. Normalizing is a floor rather than a two-sided clamp -- a negative exposure, intensity or distance comes up to zero, gamma has a floor of 0.01 because dividing by it is what gamma is for, and a colour-grade strength above one comes down because a grade is a fraction -- while CNA's own defaults pass through completely unchanged, field for field. The enums are validated rather than clamped: an undefined render or shadow quality is refused with CNA's own result, because guessing which tier a caller meant would be worse than saying so. The quality preset sets how much work each pass does and never which passes run: bloom iterations and ambient-occlusion samples rise strictly across the four tiers, eight samples to sixty-four, and every enable flag is left exactly as the caller had it. The settings text is semicolon-separated key=value pairs, and the count it answers is the point -- five of five recognised, one of three when two are typos, none for empty text or a value that will not parse -- so a caller can tell a settings file that loaded from one that did not. A loaded value goes through the same clamping a written one does, which is the trap a stale gamma of zero in a file would otherwise walk straight past. Four planted binding defects fail and none survives

entries.operation: The cascaded, spot and cube shadow passes, beside the flat one
entries.evidence: each of the three checked against the pure maths beside it, which touches no pass at all. A cascade's split distances are the ones ComputeCascadeSplitDistances returns for the same camera and lambda, twice over with two lambdas that give different answers -- and a lambda of zero divides the range evenly, which the test writes down as a closed form. The splits stay where the camera put them when the light moves, while every cascade transform moves with it, which is the separation the update is for. A spot map's light view-projection is ComputeSpotLightView times ComputeSpotLightProjection for the same light, multiplied by the test itself, and it carries real translation terms rather than being an identity that would agree with anything. A cube's face size is the cube route's answer for its tier and not the flat route's. Snapping is a pure function checked against its own definition: every axis lands on a whole number of the cascade's texels, never moves further than one, and the axis the light looks along is untouched. On a windowed OPENGLES3 renderer under Xvfb the atlas is surveyed slice by slice at six steps, so what is asserted is the change at each one: a fresh atlas is untouched storage rather than a cleared one, the first pass clears every cascade, a cast into cascade zero changes that slice alone, a later cast into the last changes only that one and leaves the first exactly as it was -- which is what says a Begin clears its own viewport rather than the atlas. A spot pass renders a floor and then the same floor raised towards the light: nearer records a smaller depth and covers more of the cone. All six cube faces open and close. HEADLESS compiles no caster program, so all three still allocate their storage and accept the passes they cannot fill while refusing their effects by name -- except the cube, whose faces are larger than that renderer's back buffer, which it says in a message carried by CNA_RESULT_INTERNAL. Twenty-two planted binding defects were run and twenty-one fail; the survivor is recorded rather than hidden, because upstream finding 16 is exactly why it cannot fail

entries.operation: The clipboard's reads, the attached-device inventory and an ungated power reading
entries.evidence: Run against both renderers, asserting a different thing about each, because the interesting claim differs. On OPENGLES3/SDL3 under Xvfb the clipboard round-trips exactly -- including non-ASCII, written and read back byte for byte -- one mouse and one keyboard are enumerated with the platform's own names and distinct identifiers, and the power route reports a state rather than an error. On HEADLESS every one of them answers *emptily and successfully*: the clipboard reads an empty string, nothing is enumerated, and the power state is Unknown -- which is the evidence that nothing here fabricates a device. The reason this family is worth having is that CNA does not gate it on the extended device layer: the windowed library used here is built with CNA_DEVICES=OFF, so cna_power_get_*_ext answers NOT_SUPPORTED on it while cna_power_get_info reports a real 79% battery, and the clipboard reads work where the extension's own write refuses. SetClipboardText now prefers the extension's write for its acceptance flag and falls back to the ungated one, so a build without the layer can write the clipboard it can already read; both routes wrap one platform clipboard, which CNA's header states. Neither answer claims the clipboard changed -- that is what the reads are for

entries.operation: The clustered forward BRDF and its volume absorption
entries.evidence: the shading model is published as a pure route, so the acceptance is a second implementation of it: a Cook-Torrance BRDF with a GGX distribution, a Smith-Schlick geometry term and a Schlick Fresnel, plus the sheen, clearcoat, iridescence and subsurface layers, written out in the test from the model and compared against CNA's at fifteen parameter combinations -- head-on, off to the side and grazing, each layer alone and all of them at once -- agreeing to two parts in a thousand everywhere. The comparison is asserted not to be vacuous: fourteen of the fifteen results are distinct, and each optional layer is asserted to change the answer, so no branch of the reference is dead. A rough sheen is used deliberately, because the lobe's width is one over max(roughness squared, 0.07) and a smooth one is too narrow to reach a grazing geometry at all -- physics, not a defect. Around the comparison: a light past its range, behind the surface, exactly at the surface, or a spot pointing away adds exactly zero; intensity is an exact multiplier; and the light's colour scales each channel and nothing else. The same BRDF driven from a PbrMaterialExtensions set is asserted to give byte-identical answers to the one driven directly, neutral and clearcoated. Volume absorption is Beer-Lambert: at a thickness equal to the attenuation distance the answer IS the attenuation colour, three times as thick cubes it, a white volume absorbs nothing, a zero distance or thickness absorbs nothing, and black is clamped off zero rather than having its logarithm taken. Six planted binding defects fail and none survives

entries.operation: The clustered light buffer, the GPU assignment and the forward effect's state
entries.evidence: the buffer's three counts are checked against the three objects it was uploaded from rather than against numbers: its light count equals the set's, its cluster count equals the grid's, and its reference count equals the assignment's own total summed over clusters -- three lights, sixty-four clusters, eighty-eight references in the fixture, and the assignment behind it is the CPU path already qualified separately. An assignment can also be adopted from the compressed-row arrays it really is, and the two clusters it describes come back holding the lights its offsets bracket, in the order the indices gave. The GPU assignment says whether it is supported and why not, and reports whether the last run really used compute rather than falling back -- both false before anything has run, which is the honest answer. The forward effect's own state round-trips at float precision, a probe and an extension set and an opaque frame each attach and detach, and a fresh effect turns out to own a neutral extension set already so the four KHR layers are always addressable. The shader is a counted borrow: CNA refuses to destroy the effect while one is outstanding, and finding that is what fixed a real defect in this binding -- Dispose used to clear its handle before the destroy, so a refused destroy stranded the effect and made the game undestroyable. It now gives the handle up only once the destroy has succeeded, and a second attempt after the borrow goes back works

entries.operation: The debug drawer: lines, shapes and light gizmos, read back as geometry
entries.evidence: everything the drawer draws is a line list and cna_debug_draw_copy_vertices hands the whole list back, so what a gizmo consists of is read rather than looked at -- which is why this family needs no renderer to be qualified. A line is exactly its two endpoints in order; a cross is three lines reaching its size along each axis and nowhere else; a box is twelve edges over eight corners, asserted as the exact ordered edge list over a box asymmetric in all three axes so that a swapped Min and Max is a different picture rather than the same corners reordered, with each corner used by exactly three edges. A sphere is three rings of its segment count, every vertex exactly on the sphere and on one of the three axis planes through its centre, and twice the segments is twice the lines; a BoundingSphere draws exactly what the same centre and radius draw. A frustum's twelve edges use all eight of the corners BoundingFrustum gives for the same matrix and nothing else -- a second independent implementation, as with the frustum culler. The gizmos are checked against the light they describe: a point light is a sphere at exactly its range plus a cross, a spot light is two cones whose rims are at range times the tangent of the outer and the inner angle on the plane the range reaches, and a directional light is an arrow starting a length back along its direction with a head a fixed fraction of that length. The depth-tested and overlay lists are separate and keep their own colours including alpha, the line count is both together, clearing empties both, and beginning a frame starts it empty. Seven planted binding defects fail and none survives

entries.operation: The depth/normal prepass: linear depth and view-space normals, rasterised and read back
entries.evidence: accepted against CNA's own rasteriser on a windowed OPENGLES3 renderer under Xvfb. One flat quad is drawn twice in the same frame into render targets of the same size, read back by the same routine: once through a stock BasicEffect, which shares no code with the prepass, and once through the prepass itself. The two rectangles agree to within 1.5 texels on every edge, so this renderer's screen and readback conventions cancel between them and what is left is whether the prepass puts the scene where the renderer puts it. The depth is exact rather than merely below the far plane: a quad at view depth 10 with a far plane of 100 reads back as the number CNA's own pack and unpack routes give for 0.1 through an eight-bit target, to five decimals, and the whole buffer holds exactly two values -- that surface and the far-plane clear -- with the surface count equal to the covered texel count. The normals are exact too: every covered texel carries (128, 128, 255), which is +Z in view space encoded, with the alpha that marks a texel as carrying no velocity. An untouched normal texel carries the depth buffer's white, because one clear serves a bound target set. Roughness round-trips and clamps into the unit range at both ends; the pass count agrees with the multiple-render-target answer; velocity is off and its texture is null rather than an empty buffer; and both prepass programs are lent and are real. Two findings came out of it: the packed encoding delivers one part in 255 rather than the documented one part in 2^24 once it is stored in the eight-bit target it is written for, which the test measures with a sweep and a 256-level control (upstream finding 13), and three of its ordering refusals answer INTERNAL where the header documents INVALID_STATE (upstream finding 14). Both are asserted as they behave, so a repair fails and says so

entries.operation: The glTF material bridge, and the one conversion it performs
entries.evidence: the bridge is the only thing in this family that converts rather than carries: a glTF base-colour factor is a linear float vector and a CNA albedo is an eight-bit colour. That conversion is measured over a table of seven inputs rather than from one point, and every one matches round(x * 255) -- (1, 0.5, 0.25, 0.5) becomes (255, 128, 64, 128). Everything else is asserted to arrive unchanged, each factor set to a value no default equals, and the per-slot values are asserted to arrive in their own slot and nowhere else: one coordinate set written to the emissive slot leaves the other six at zero, and one transform written to the metallic-roughness slot leaves the other six neutral. The extension bridge is checked the same way against a fresh extension set. glTF's own defaults come from CNA rather than from numbers written here, so a change upstream is a diagnostic rather than a silent difference

entries.operation: The Guide's two asynchronous screens, and CNA's own answers to them
entries.evidence: Guide.BeginShowMessageBox and Guide.BeginShowKeyboardInput are the only genuinely asynchronous begin/end pairs in XNA, and both now work. A message box does not complete inside the Begin call and says so, carries the caller's async state untouched, makes Guide.IsVisible true, and holds the focus button XNA was given rather than a default. Answering it runs the continuation exactly once with the very result object Begin returned -- the IAsyncResult contract -- and EndShowMessageBox returns the button that was pressed; a second box with a different press returns that one instead, so the answer is not a constant. The keyboard input reports its title, description and starting text back from CNA, and a cancel makes EndShowKeyboardInput return null rather than an empty string, which is XNA's distinction. A second screen while one is pending is INVALID_STATE, and End before the answer is an error rather than a wait. Three planted defects fail: a dropped focus button, an End that accepts a foreign or incomplete result, and a continuation that fires twice. Nothing here fabricates a gamer, a sign-in or a peer: CNA draws the screen and answers it, which is the same deterministic injection the sensors and the camera use

entries.operation: The HDR display transfer chain: PQ, the wide-gamut primaries, the highlight roll-off, and their composition
entries.evidence: CNA publishes the whole chain as pure routes, so what a frame will look like is checked without a display that can show it -- and each part is checked against the standard it implements rather than against a run. The PQ curve is SMPTE ST 2084 written out from the standard's own five constants at nine brightnesses, clamped at ten thousand nits and at zero rather than extrapolated or negated, monotone across its range, and an exact inverse of its decode. Half the signal is spent below a hundred nits, which is what a perceptual quantiser is for. The primaries are the BT.2087 matrix, checked on the three Rec.709 primaries, white, black and a mixture: white stays white because the rows sum to one, black stays black, a Rec.709 red becomes a less saturated mixture in the wider gamut, and the conversion is linear. The roll-off turned out to be Reinhard against the peak rather than a knee -- a hundred nits against a thousand-nit peak comes back as ninety-one -- so it pulls everything down a little, approaches the peak without reaching it however large the input, and is strictly rising throughout; the binding's own comment was corrected to say so. The composition is the claim worth making, and it is bit-identical rather than close: brightness and the roll-off happen FIRST, in the source primaries, and only then is the gamut converted and the curve applied. Rolling off after the conversion gives a different answer, which the test also asserts so the ordering claim is not vacuous. An sRGB display gets the scene value unchanged -- proved twice, once from the pure route and once as a byte-exact drawn frame on a windowed renderer -- and scRGB gets it scaled against the eighty-nit reference white

entries.operation: The instanced renderer: uploading transforms and tints, and which draw path ran
entries.evidence: Built over one XNB-loaded ModelMeshPart, which the renderer borrows and this object keeps alive. The instance buffer is measured rather than trusted: uploading three then two lowers the count to two while the capacity does not fall, which is CNA reusing the buffer rather than reallocating, and an empty upload is accepted as the documented way to stop drawing without destroying the renderer. Drawing is qualified on what it says it did, not on success: HEADLESS answers false to is_instancing_supported, so with the fallback off the draw refuses, and with it on two instances produce two draw calls with did_last_draw_instance false -- the observable that separates a per-instance loop from one instanced call. The refusal arrives as INTERNAL rather than the documented INVALID_STATE; that is upstream finding 25, reproduced in pure C first and asserted here so a repair fails the assertion and says so. No pixel claim is made on HEADLESS

entries.operation: The last of the engine layer: indirect draws, the frame's two scenes, and the odds
entries.evidence: the indirect command format is the GPU's own, and it is pinned as bytes: four words for a draw and five for an indexed one, in the order the GPU reads them, with a SIGNED base vertex -- minus five packs to 0xFFFFFFFB and reads back as minus five, which a clamp to zero or an unsigned coercion cannot do. The defaults are all zero, which draws nothing, and a default cullable instance's world is a ZERO matrix rather than the identity its header promises (finding 23, in a third place) while the empty box beside it is exact. The memory-barrier membership test is checked across seven bits with three masks -- a mask of bits 0, 2 and 4 contains exactly those three, an empty mask contains nothing, a full one contains everything -- so a test that answered a constant or ignored its second argument fails. The frame's TWO scene callbacks are qualified as a sequence: both are off by default and neither runs however it was registered, because the pipeline skips a phase rather than drawing into nothing; with transparency and shadows switched on both run, and the ORDER is the frame's own -- casters inside Begin, transparent inside End, which is why they are two routes rather than one list. Clearing one leaves the other running. The scene bounds really cross: two boxes ten times apart produce two different light transforms on the shadow map that recorded them. A callback that throws stops the frame and its OWN exception object reaches the caller of End. The post-process chain lends its own render-target pool -- a target acquired through it appears in the chain's pool, and the chain refuses release while the borrowed view is out. The .cube loader reads a table this test wrote, at the size and title the file gave it, and both of its failure modes -- a path that does not exist and a file that is not a .cube -- come back as NOT_SUPPORTED, the code every other route uses for a missing engine layer (finding 24, diagnosed to a catch clause naming a sibling class). Ten planted binding defects fail and none survives

entries.operation: The native model-mesh-part side-car a managed ModelMeshPart lends CNA
entries.evidence: The subject is a real XNB-loaded Model read through the strict ContentManager, so what is measured is the object a consumer actually holds. The claim that matters is that no geometry is uploaded twice: cna_model_mesh_part_create retains the buffers it is given rather than copying them, and the native part is asked for its vertex and index buffers and hands back the same handles the managed VertexBuffer and IndexBuffer own -- checked against the live handles, not assumed. All four scalars round-trip, and the bridge refuses its own side-car at creation if any of them disagrees, so an upstream change that stopped preserving one surfaces as an error rather than as geometry drawn from the wrong offset. Identity is a WeakMap on the public object: borrowing twice yields one native part, and reaching the same part through the collection again yields that same one. The disposal order is the trap and is asserted separately: CNA refuses to destroy a buffer a part retains (INVALID_STATE, measured in pure C), so a side-car that outlived its buffers would break XNA's IDisposable contract. The teardown hangs on the buffer's NativeResourceLifetime rather than on GraphicsResource.Dispose, because the game lifetime also cascades to its children and that path never touches the wrapper -- disposing the managed VertexBuffer succeeds, and re-borrowing afterwards names ObjectDisposedException

entries.operation: The particle draw: live particles painted where the camera puts them
entries.evidence: accepted on the texels the draw painted into a render target on a windowed OPENGLES3 renderer under Xvfb. The scene is made predictable rather than guessed at: the simulation is pinned to the CPU, every source of variance is zero and the emitter's speed is zero, so all 32 particles stand exactly on the emitter -- which the pool, read back, confirms is the one point and no other. Two systems at different world positions with different particle sizes are drawn through one camera the test built itself from CreateLookAt and CreateOrthographic, and each painted region is checked against where that camera puts that emitter and how wide that particle size is there: both squares land within 1.5 texels on every edge, cover their predicted area to within 20%, and are painted in the particle texture's colour and no other. Drawing either system alone puts its square in the same place, a system with an emission rate of zero paints nothing at all and does not fail, and moving the camera two world units slides both squares by exactly what the new view predicts. CNA's default capacity comes from the route that takes no capacity and is 1024, which tools/cna-abi/contract.json pins to CNA's own header with a _Static_assert, and the storage-buffer binding point the API states is the one CNA's own particle GLSL declares. Nine planted binding defects fail, including a draw that swaps the view and the projection, one that sends the view as both, one that drops the texture, a settings setter that loses the particle size, and a softness setter that never reaches CNA. One survives and is recorded as unkillable: creating at the default capacity by asking for 1024 explicitly is indistinguishable from asking CNA, because no route says which was used. The soft-particle fade is the one thing not accepted -- the depth image and the softness reach CNA and change nothing that is drawn, which is upstream finding 12, asserted as it currently behaves so a repair is noticed

entries.operation: The particle simulation, and the pure functions behind it
entries.evidence: cna_particle_system_step integrates one particle with no system, device or GPU, and cna_particle_system_random is the deterministic generator the emitter draws from -- so the simulation is checked against arithmetic rather than against numbers recorded from a run. Gravity of -10 over half a second gives velocity -5 and position -2.5 exactly, an axis with no gravity is unchanged, and the age advances by the step. Two half steps and one whole step both reach velocity -10 but land in different places, which is what shows the elapsed time reaching a stepwise integrator rather than being ignored; a zero step changes nothing; and Step returns a new particle rather than mutating the caller's. The same seed always draws the same value and different seeds draw different ones. The system itself round-trips its emitter settings through a different route than they went in, reports its capacity, and says whether it is simulating on the GPU and why not -- forced onto the CPU here, which is how a game gets the same answer on every renderer. Three planted defects fail: a fixed step, a seed that never reaches the generator, and gravity that is always the default

entries.operation: The physically-based effects, skinned and not, and the material they carry
entries.evidence: the acceptance is two independent paths into one state. A whole material goes on with one route, and every field is then read back through the per-field accessors -- routes the apply never touched -- before the extractor is asked for the material again and CNA's own equality compares it with what went on. The per-field setters then move the same state, which is what makes those two paths two rather than one. A fresh effect starts at exactly the material's own defaults, which is what makes them one type. Per-slot state is asserted to land in its own slot: a coordinate set and a transform written to the normal slot arrive there and the base-colour slot keeps its own, and an sRGB flag cleared on one slot leaves the others set. The skinned effect carries the same material and its own skeleton: four bone weights per vertex by default, a translation and a scale that survive the round trip, identity that stays identity, and a request for fewer bones than were set answering with that many. On a windowed renderer both are real compiled effects with named techniques whose passes execute, which HEADLESS constructs and refuses. The texture slots are upstream finding 19 and are asserted as measured rather than as documented

entries.operation: The rest of the post-process passes: tonemapping, depth of field, lens flare, motion blur, chromatic aberration and film grain
entries.evidence: every pass is checked against something that is not the pass. The tonemapper is the clearest case: CNA ships the curve twice, once as the shader and once as cna_tonemap_pass_tonemap_channel on the CPU, and the headless suite first pins that CPU route to the published closed forms -- Reinhard is exactly v/(1+v), ACES is the Narkowicz fit, None is a clamp not a curve, exposure multiplies before the curve and gamma raises after it -- and the windowed suite then predicts every channel of every texel of a drawn frame through it, at five different settings that produce five different frames. Bloom's extraction is a soft knee, not the subtraction its comment used to claim: measured at (0.8, 0.8) it returns 0.2, a quarter of the channel, and the headless test now predicts the whole ramp from the knee's shape and checks monotonicity in both value and threshold. Depth of field's circle of confusion is checked against the thin-lens equation written out in the test, at five lens settings: it is zero at the focus distance, symmetric about it, and opening two stops doubles it exactly. Each pass's own off switch is an exact identity on a real GPU -- a bloom of no intensity, a bloom whose threshold is above every channel, a flare of either, a blur of no strength, an aberration of no strength, grain of no intensity, and the layer's own blit -- eight of them, all byte-exact. Turned on, each must change the frame in the way its name means: a bloom only ever adds light, chromatic aberration moves red and blue and leaves green untouched at every texel, grain changes most of the frame by amounts that differ per texel rather than a constant offset, and FXAA leaves the smooth interior alone and touches the border it clamps at. The GLSL the layer hands out is never compared against a dialect: what is asserted is that each source is a real program, that the packed-depth SSAO variant is a different program from the plain one, and that the iridescence source is the function library it claims to be

entries.operation: The retro effects: a CRT shader, an ASCII quantiser and a depth-quantising effect
entries.evidence: the CRT is drawn through the layer's own fullscreen pass over a flat grey source, so what comes back is the pattern the shader adds and nothing else. With all four parameters at zero it is a byte-exact copy, which is what makes each later change attributable. Scanlines darken alternate rows by exactly the intensity -- 200 becomes 100 at 0.5 and 150 at 0.25, on every texel of every second row, with the rows between untouched -- and a vignette is verified as radial rather than as recorded numbers: symmetric under both mirrors at all 64 texels, strictly brightening along the diagonal towards the centre, a corner below half the source and a centre above nine tenths of it. Every CRT parameter is written with a value that differs from the default it replaces, so a setter that did nothing is caught rather than agreeing with itself. The ASCII effect's grid is the source size over the cell size and never the destination's: a 32x24 source drawn into a rectangle four times its area gives 4x2 in 8x12 cells, 8x6 in 4x4 and 2x3 in 16x8, each checked against that division, and 0x0 before anything has been quantised. An AsciiPass lends its own effect, and writing a cell size through the borrow changes the pass's own. The depth effect is qualified as native state rather than pixels and says so: it quantises a depth input a colour blit does not supply, so its mode and dither round-trip through CNA and no picture is claimed

entries.operation: The shadow depth pass: casters rendered into a shadow map, and the depths read back
entries.evidence: accepted on the depth texels a real pass produced on a windowed OPENGLES3 renderer under Xvfb, against a prediction the test computes rather than a measurement copied out of a run. The pass transform is cross-checked first: the light view-projection CNA reports for an open pass equals the product of ComputeLightView and ComputeLightProjection -- two pure routes that take the same light and scene box and touch no shadow map -- multiplied in the test itself, so three CNA routes and one local identity have to agree. Then the geometry: one asymmetric quad inside an asymmetric scene box, projected corner by corner through that matrix into texels and depth, and every prediction checked against the rendering. An empty pass leaves all 262144 texels at exactly 1.0; the occluder darkens exactly the predicted rectangle to within 1.5 texels on each edge and fills 98% of its area; the recorded depth is the projected depth to within 1e-5; two heights eight units apart differ by exactly the projection's depth scale times eight and cover identical texels; and the same draw outside Begin/End reaches none of the map, which is what shows End unbinding it. The two lent caster programs are told apart by what they rasterise -- the skinned one writes nothing from vertices carrying no bone weights -- because their handles cannot tell them apart: CNA hands out a fresh handle for every borrow. Borrows are counted: the map refuses destruction while one is outstanding, so each is taken once and returned before the map. Fifteen planted binding defects fail, including a dropped scene box, a negated light direction, an End that reports success without closing the pass, either caster getter wired to the other route, a depth texture re-borrowed on every read, and a Dispose that destroys the map before returning its borrows

entries.operation: The shadow-receiver contract: the lighting and shadow state an effect carries
entries.evidence: these are not properties of one class, because CNA hangs them off the Effect handle itself -- and that is shown rather than asserted: THREE effects give THREE different answers. A stock BasicEffect is a shadow receiver and NOT an image-based-light receiver; a PbrEffect is both; a ShaderEffect is neither and refuses every route with INVALID_ARGUMENT rather than accepting values nothing will read. Every documented default is checked field by field -- kind NONE, the origin, direction (0,-1,0), white, range 20, inner 0.35, outer 0.5, bias 0.004, no textures, zero cascades, four zero splits, no blend band, no debug tint -- and every one is exact except the transforms, which the header calls identity and which are ZERO matrices in all six places they appear. That is finding 23, and the implementation is the half that is right: its own comments say a defaulted C state must match a defaulted C++ one, where Matrix() is value-initialised to zeros. Asserted as measured, so making the documentation true by moving the code fails the test. The cascade array is a FIXED FOUR whatever the count says: two transforms given come back as two plus two defaults, a count of three with one transform given keeps the init's defaults in the other two rather than whatever the effect held before, and a fifth transform or a count outside the array is refused by name. Every setter writes a value different from the default it replaces, so one that never reached CNA is caught. The punctual light's two shadow textures come back as nothing WHATEVER was set -- the canonical structure holds raw pointers and this ABI will not invent a handle for a texture it does not track -- while every other field of the same structure round-trips, which is what makes that an asymmetry rather than a getter returning defaults. The image-based light's completeness test is checked from both sides: a light with no textures is not valid, and more mips do not make it so, because the textures are what is missing. Eleven planted binding defects were run: ten fail, and the survivor is recorded as equivalent under this ABI with the reason

entries.operation: The two engine-layer caches: render targets by shape, shader effects by name
entries.evidence: the pool's key is all FIVE arguments, each shown on its own to make a different target: size, surface format, depth format and slot, with the same five returning the one target the pool already holds. The non-square case is asked for deliberately, because a pool handed its size the wrong way round returns a transposed target that costs exactly the same bytes. The byte estimate is COLOUR ONLY -- 8x8 Color is 256 bytes, and adding a half-float target of the same size costs 512, so the estimate reads each entry's own format rather than assuming one; the depth buffers the targets also carry are not counted, which makes it a floor rather than the whole cost. On a windowed renderer the identity is proved by PIXELS rather than by counting: painted through one borrow and read back through a second borrow of the same key, while the neighbouring slot holds its own different colour. The factory's key is the NAME ALONE, and that is shown rather than described -- a second acquire under a cached name draws the CACHED shader even when handed different source, so a caller who edits a shader and keeps the name silently keeps the old one; the same edited source under a NEW name really does compile and really does draw, so the assertion is about the cache and not about a shader that never worked. The compile count survives Clear, because it counts compiles rather than entries, which is what makes it useful for noticing a name rebuilt every frame. Both caches LEND what they hold: reset, clear and destroy are all refused with INVALID_STATE while a borrow is outstanding and all succeed once every borrow is back, and the probe game destroying cleanly is itself the proof that every borrow was returned. A non-positive size is INVALID_ARGUMENT rather than INVALID_STATE, and an empty cache key is refused by this binding before CNA sees it. Ten planted binding defects fail and none survives

entries.operation: The volumetric and atmospheric screen-space passes: aerial perspective, height fog, light shafts and volumetric fog
entries.evidence: three of the four publish the arithmetic their shader runs as a pure C route, and that is where the acceptance is. Air mass is checked against Kasten-Young written out from the published formula at ten directions and distances -- one atmosphere straight up, about thirty-eight along the horizon, linear in distance until that ceiling, clamped at zero for a negative distance, and a zero-length direction treated as straight up rather than divided by. Transmittance is checked against Rayleigh per channel plus a grey Mie term at seven turbidities and air masses: no air takes nothing, blue is scattered hardest, and more aerosol takes more light while narrowing the spread between channels, which is why haze washes colour out rather than tinting it. Height fog's optical depth is the closed form of the integral the shader marches, checked at ten configurations and in all three of its branches: no fog at all, a level ray that accumulates linearly, and a climbing ray that converges while a descending one runs away. Moving the layer up with the camera puts the answer back exactly. On a windowed renderer each pass's own off setting is a byte-exact copy -- five of them -- and turned on, the fog moves every texel monotonically towards its own colour and never past it, a descending camera gathers more than a level one at the same density, and enough density gives exactly the fog colour. Eight planted binding defects fail and none survives

entries.operation: Transparency: the back-to-front draw list, and the weighted-blended resolve that needs no order at all
entries.evidence: the sorted list is a pure CPU object, so the whole ordering is qualified without a renderer. The camera a view matrix implies is checked against this package's own Matrix.Invert on six views including two with a scale in them -- and the rigid-view shortcut, written out in the test, is shown to disagree on the scaled ones and to agree on the rigid ones, so the scaled cases are the assertion they claim to be. The sort key is the distance to the NEAREST POINT of the box, checked against a float clamp-into-box reference on seven boxes and pinned at the three places it differs from the mistakes it is confused with: a camera inside the box sorts at zero, a box off two axes is measured to its corner, and a large shell around the camera sorts at zero rather than at its half-diagonal. The order is farthest-first and STABLE: two draws at the same distance keep submission order, asserted against a stable descending sort written out in the test rather than borrowed, repeated eight times, and shown to change with the camera. DrawSorted runs the callbacks in exactly that order, and a callback that throws stops the draw where it failed, propagates its own exception object rather than a wrapper, and leaves the list usable. The OIT weight is McGuire and Bavoil's, predicted in float in CNA's own order over seventeen cases: the ceiling is taken exactly at the eye, the depth clamp makes everything past the far plane weigh the same, alpha is a linear factor, the curve decreases across 200 samples, and the published lower clamp is shown to be UNREACHABLE once z is clamped to one -- recorded rather than asserted live. A zero far plane is guarded rather than dividing by zero. The bracket opens on EVERY renderer including one that cannot resolve, which is CNA's corrected behaviour and the opposite of what its header still documents (finding 21); the state machine refuses a second Begin, a resize under itself and a resolve while accumulating, each with the result code that names the kind of mistake. On a windowed renderer both lent targets are half-float, the same shape, resize together, and read back as HalfVector4 zeros; an empty resolve then DISCARDS rather than blending a zero contribution, leaving the target exactly as it was cleared -- measured inside one binding, because binding a render target discards what it held and an earlier clear would have been gone. The accumulation half is qualified to the pixel through a custom shader calling cnaOitEmit: two overlapping layers at very different depths accumulate exactly what McGuire and Bavoil's weight predicts on the CPU, the revealage target holds the SUM of the logs rather than the product of the transmissions, and the resolve divides them into the near layer's own colour at three quarters coverage -- 64,128,255,191, predicted channel by channel and matched exactly. Eleven planted binding defects fail and none survives

entries.operation: Typed text, IME composition and the mouse cursor
entries.evidence: The one input family CNA pushes rather than letting a game poll, because composition is: an IME sends editing updates and candidate lists between the keystroke and the committed character, none of which fits a per-frame snapshot. XNA had no concept of any of it -- Keyboard.GetState reports physical keys, a different question from what the user typed the moment the layout is not US English. Driven through CNA's own _ext injection hooks, which is injection evidence rather than hardware evidence and says so. Nothing assumes ASCII: 'a', 'e-acute', two CJK ideographs and U+1F600 are delivered as six UTF-16 code units -- the emoji as the surrogate pair the platform actually sends -- and appending them rebuilds the text exactly; five characters from six code units. Composition text round-trips as UTF-8 with its selection start and length kept apart, and candidate lists keep their order, selection and orientation. A disposed subscription receives nothing further, and an exception thrown out of a handler is contained at the boundary rather than unwound into compiled C, with a later subscriber still running. Start, Stop, the typed start and the input rectangle all succeed while IsActive stays false, because HEADLESS has no window to start input on -- measured, not assumed. A cursor is an owned handle that closes and releases in that order and refuses after disposal. Three planted defects each fail the test: a code unit truncated to a byte, a composition Length reported as its Start, and an unsubscribe that never reaches CNA

entries.operation: VideoPlayer.GetTexture borrowed frame projection and its decode identity
entries.evidence: cna_video_player_get_frame_ext's monotonic decode generation is what made a safe projection possible: GetTexture now hands back a non-owning Texture2D over the player's own frame, returns the same object while the generation is unchanged, and retires it the moment anything else touches the player -- the exact window CNA says the handle is valid for. entries.operation: Windowed Linux qualification: real GPU pixels through the public XNA drawing path
entries.evidence: against an OPENGLES3/SDL3 CNA library under Xvfb, a RenderTarget2D cleared to (12, 34, 56, 255) through GraphicsDevice.Clear reads back all sixteen texels exactly, the renderer reports itself as OPENGLES3 with a 16384-texel limit and 0x7ffff capability flags, a stock BasicEffect pass applies for real rather than returning the HEADLESS not-supported branch, and 60 and 600 SpriteBatch frames run without drift. Opt-in through CNA_WINDOWED_LIBRARY, and it skips with a reason where no windowed library or display exists

entries.operation: Windowed qualification across three renderers, with GameWindow and adapter state
entries.evidence: The windowed suite now runs against every renderer it is pointed at and has been run against three: OPENGLES3, SDL_RENDERER and SOFTWARE, all ABI 0.21 and all under Xvfb. Each reports its own identity, capability flags and texture limit; each applies a stock BasicEffect for real; each runs 60 and 600 frames. GameWindow is exercised where HEADLESS cannot reach it: a title written and read back and restored, a native handle that stays a bigint, a screen device name, an orientation, and AllowUserResizing flipped and restored. Client bounds are measured rather than assumed, because the renderers disagree honestly -- OPENGLES3 and SDL_RENDERER report the 320x240 the manager requested, SOFTWARE reports 0x0 because it presents through a surface -- so what is asserted is that a renderer reporting a client area reports the requested one. SDL_RENDERER and SOFTWARE produce the exact sixteen render-target texels; OPENGLES3 no longer does, and that regression is asserted as measured rather than skipped, so its repair fails the test. See docs/upstream-cna-findings.md item 7

entries.operation: Browser GamePad: connection, capabilities, buttons, thumbsticks and triggers
entries.evidence: test/wasm-browser-input.mjs drives GamePad.GetState/GetCapabilities from inside an ordinary XNA Update in headless Chromium. With no controller attached all four PlayerIndex slots report IsConnected false rather than an invented device; with a Gamepad API device emulated at the browser boundary -- the integration point SDL3's Emscripten joystick driver actually reads -- the capability table, A and D-pad button states, both thumbstick axes with CNA's Y-inversion, the analog left trigger and an advancing PacketNumber all arrive, and releasing returns every one of them to zero. SetVibration reports false, because the browser's standard mapping exposes no rumble to SDL. Three planted defects -- swapped thumbsticks, an always-connected capability table and a previous-position that reports the current one -- each fail exactly one of these tests

entries.operation: Browser TouchPanel: the touch collection and XNA's press/move/release states
entries.evidence: test/wasm-browser-input.mjs dispatches real Chromium touch events and reads TouchPanel.GetState from inside Update. Before the first finger there is no touch device at all, which is distinct from a device with nothing on it. A press arrives as TouchLocationState.Pressed with no previous location, the next frame is Moved at the same point, a move keeps the identifier and reports the press position as its previous one, a second finger is Pressed while the first stays Moved, and lifting reports Released exactly once before the collection empties. The XNA enumerator visits the same identifiers in the same order as the indexer

entries.evidence: the same two schemas over the WebAssembly backend, and the one that settles a wasm32 convention with evidence: cna_curve_key_collection_add takes CNA_CurveKey **by value**, and cna_cnb_encode_animation_clip takes a descriptor holding a pointer to an array of descriptors each holding a pointer to an array of 48-byte keyframes. The container primitives agree across backends too: the CRC-32C check value and the magic are the same C routines either side

entries.operation: CNB media in a browser, including a measured sound-effect duration

The browser artifact is built with SDL3 audio rather than NULL, so this is where the sound effect's duration is actually measurable: a quarter second of 8 kHz mono PCM16 encoded to .cnb, decoded back and turned into an XNA SoundEffect reports exactly 250 ms and 2,500,000 ticks, which is arithmetic on the frame count and therefore exact evidence that the samples and the rate both survived. Both loop numbers, the sample bytes, and the song and video descriptions are asserted as on Node

entries.operation: CNB model in a browser: the same schema, on the WebAssembly backend
entries.evidence: a page builds a model with CnbModelData, encodes it with CNA's own writer and decodes it back, asserting the same values the Node suite asserts: both bone parents and both transforms, the part's stride and its exact vertex and index payloads through wasm32 memory, two named texture slots beside a third left empty, the mesh's parent bone and part list, all three skeleton matrix sets kept apart by their own diagonals, and the baked light. The structure layouts are measured by the same Emscripten probe as the rest, never hand-written. A planted defect that ignored the skeleton matrix-set identity fails this test; a second, which returned zero for every bone parent, passed until the test was strengthened to sample the root bone as well as the child -- so the gate is known to be able to fail for both

entries.operation: CNB's writers produce identical bytes on both backends

A browser page builds the same 52-byte payload and the same 326-byte container from the same calls, and the test compares the payload against the exact little-endian layout the desktop ABI produces rather than against the page agreeing with itself. The read-limits structure crosses through a wasm32 layout measured by an Emscripten probe, not a handwritten one
